$comment: Blocks retired from public/content/ under hard rule 1a of the visual compaction brief, and the
figure that took over each one's job.
RULE 1a, IN FULL: an ASCII or box-drawing diagram, a pseudo-table inside a code block, a stack
of near-identical cards or a restated 'summary' table may be deleted ONCE a figure renders the
same facts. A visual takes over the job only when it shows every fact, number, tier label and
source the text it replaces carried — and every figure keeps a 'View the data' disclosure
generated from its data file, so the numbers stay on the page and stay in the printed PDF.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. scripts/verify-content-integrity.mjs compares every body line against the
baseline and fails the build on anything that moved, which is exactly right: the restructure
moved body text, it did not rewrite it. A retirement is the one thing this brief authorises
that the guard cannot tell apart from a quiet deletion. Declaring it costs one entry and a
sentence saying which figure carries the facts — the same bargain notation-rewrites.json
strikes for prose, and scripts/figure-migrations.json for figures leaving the markdown.
`facts` is not decoration. It is the checklist the figure is held to, and Phase 8's report
itemises the words retired against it. If a fact listed here is not visible in the figure or in
its 'View the data' table, the retirement is not authorised and the block goes back.

`blocks` is how many fenced blocks the entry retires — omit it for one. The three §3.6 section banners are one entry covering three blocks, so the fence-delimiter allowance has to count blocks and not entries.

facts: Registered electorate: 532,758 voters across 40 wards, 532,833 with prisons

retirements.note: The textbook case of the 'restated summary table' rule 1a names. Every figure in it had already been established and every one is now COMPUTED from data/ward-register.json rather than transcribed, so the summary cannot drift from what it summarises. Three of the eight lines are in dispute and the banner stated all eight in one voice: the deficit share is printed 51.72% where the register gives 51.73% (C-6), the overlap is printed '5 of top 8' where the fifth ward ranks 11th (C-5), and the mandate names 24 wards for a pool spanning 21 (C-7). The figure shows what §3.4.6 printed beside what the register says, on those three rows only, and each row names the subsection that established it — which is what makes it a way back into §3.4 rather than a second copy of it. No number in the content has been changed.

retirements.was: A box-drawing branch tree headed GOVERNOR MALOMBE'S 2027 CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS — one question forking into Branch A (disqualification) and Branch B (eligibility), each with a reading of Article 180(7) and a list of strategic consequences.
facts: The question: Governor Malombe's 2027 constitutional status under Article 180(7)
Branch A's reading: interrupted terms count toward the cumulative limit of two terms
Branch B's reading: only contiguous terms or uninterrupted service triggers the lifetime limit
Branch A's consequences: open-seat contest; intense factional realignment in Wiper; rapid shift in voter blocs and alliances; an environment for technocratic change
Branch B's consequences: Malombe defends incumbency; the campaign executes a direct anti-incumbency strategy; it must overcome active executive patronage
retirements.note: THE ONLY BLOCK IN THIS FILE WHOSE FACTS WERE ALREADY STATED TWICE ELSEWHERE, which is why it retires without a new figure being built. retirements.was: A box-drawing matrix headed TRILINGUAL AUDIENCE & CHANNEL MAPPING MATRIX — three languages with their primary demographic targets and electorate shares, dominant media channels and formats, and emotional and strategic objective.
facts: Kikamba: rural smallholder farmers (32.8%), women chamas and rural mothers (52.1%), village elders and clan leaders, agro-pastoralists (Mwingi/South); estimated primary reach ~76%
Kikamba's channels as stated: vernacular radio (Musyi, Wikwatyo), 2G bulk SMS and USSD, baraza PA addresses, megaphone audio clips
Kikamba's objective: emotional affinity, cultural authenticity and community stewardship trust
Kiswahili and Sheng: urban MSMEs, mama mbogas and traders, boda boda riders and hustlers (43.9%), inter-county commuters and transporters, semi-urban youth; ~16%
Kiswahili's channels: market PA sound trucks, TikTok and Reels video, WhatsApp group flyers, open-air town rallies
Kiswahili's objective: everyday economic solidarity, commercial dynamism and hustle dignity
English: teachers, doctors and civil servants, national press bureau chiefs, professional and corporate diaspora, judicial, EACC and regulatory bodies; ~8%
English's channels: 60-page main manifesto, statutory IEBC filings, LinkedIn and X longform, national TV interviews (Citizen, KTN, NTV)
English's objective: technocratic competence, statutory legal precision and national economic policy leadership
retirements.note: THE CHANNEL LIST IS TRANSCRIBED, NOT CORRECTED. '2G Bulk SMS & USSD' under Kikamba is C-21: §8.10.2 states, citing the Communications Authority at Tier 1, that political bulk SMS is restricted to English or Kiswahili and that an operator may refuse a non-compliant message outright — and six other places in the document agree with §8.10.2, including §7.3.4 in this same subsection, which gives the SMS rail 80% Kiswahili and 20% English and allocates Kikamba none of it. The figure prints the list as §7.3.1 gives it and carries the flag beneath it. Dropping the words quietly would have hidden the one conflict in this audit that could have a message refused by an operator after the campaign had committed a 48-hour lodging lead time. The three reach shares are stated without a citation and are rendered Tier 3, as a language map rather than a measurement.

retirements.was: A box-drawing matrix headed CHANNEL-BY-LANGUAGE DEPLOYMENT MATRIX — seven campaign output media with a primary language allocation and a secondary or supplementary one.
facts: Vernacular radio spots: 100% Kikamba, none secondary — zero English/Swahili intrusion on spots

USSD menu system: 50% Kikamba, 50% Kiswahili — toggle via option 0
Baraza print collateral: 70% Kikamba, 30% Kiswahili and English (executive summaries)
Sound PA truck jingles: 85% Kikamba, 15% Swahili/Sheng (urban market stops)
TikTok and Reels video: 50% Swahili/Sheng, 35% English, 15% Kikamba punchlines
Formal policy manifesto: 100% English, abridged 12-page summaries in Kikamba and Swahili
retirements.note: Drawn as seven separate 100% allocations rather than a grouped bar chart, because these rows do not share a scale: 100% of radio and 100% of the manifesto are two different totals, and one axis across them would invite a comparison the table never made. figures.test.ts asserts that every row allocates exactly 100%. The SMS row is the version C-21 says is right and §7.3.1 contradicts, and it carries the flag.
